purpose: Replay current F2 coordination-method candidates against recent primary research without treating literature similarity as project evidence.

sources.title: A Comprehensive Empirical Evaluation of Agent Frameworks on Code-centric Software Engineering Tasks
sources.relevance: Reports effectiveness/efficiency/overhead tradeoffs across agent frameworks and observes long trajectories/correction attempts associated with coordination overhead in one multi-agent framework.

sources.title: Verification-Aware Planning for Multi-Agent Systems
sources.relevance: Models subtask dependencies and explicit verification functions/pass criteria; reported gains support making executable verification and dependency structure first-class coordination objects.

sources.title: SWE-EVO: Benchmarking Coding Agents in Long-Horizon Software Evolution Scenarios
sources.relevance: Finds a large gap between long-horizon software evolution and isolated issue solving, supporting conservative interpretation of component-level agent success as whole-project progress.

synthesis: Current literature is directionally consistent with the project's shift from raw fan-out toward dependency-aware, verification-aware convergence.

The literature does not establish the specific F2 rule that an already queued discriminator bundle should remain stable; that rule remains a project-local method candidate and must be validated against future runtime episodes.
Do not turn external paper results into runtime, product, training, GWT/J-Space or canonical semantics credit.
Use external research to generate falsifiers and scheduling hypotheses; only project execution can promote project evidence.
recursive_test: Across future F2 runtime episodes, compare stable-probe versus superseded-probe paths on terminal evidence latency, duplicate queued jobs, executed-step yield, invalid-witness rate and exact promotion depth. Revise or retire the method if it suppresses validity-critical falsifiers or increases evidence latency.
